I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to earn a stable harvest because the climate, irrigation habits, and local selling channels all fit these two crops. I am 53, so I do not want a plan that is too complicated or too labor-intensive. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because they are easier for me to manage and give steadier yields than old local seed. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is practical, common, and cheaper than deep ploughing every season. I will put moderate fertilizer on both crops, not too little and not too much, because I want reliable output without wasting money. I will irrigate wheat more times than maize because wheat here usually needs more water support, especially around jointing and grain filling, while maize can often manage with fewer irrigations if rain is normal. I will spray only as needed for common diseases, weeds, and insects, keeping applications limited because every spray costs money and labor. My goal this year is not to chase the highest possible yield; I will aim for a stable, manageable crop plan that I can handle well and that matches local conditions.
